question.text: An offshore fund pooling capital for Indian investments may register with SEBI as an FVCI. Which of the following is a SPECIFIC flexibility available to FVCI-registered offshore funds?

answer.text: Exemption from SEBI Takeover Code in respect of shares of a company and QIB status
Right to contribute more than INR 1 crore per investor
Mandatory lock-in of 3 years on every investment

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 8.5.1: FVCI status provides flexibility in entry/exit pricing, exemption from lock-in post-IPO, exemption from SEBI Takeover Code, and QIB status in capital markets. The Trap: Option B is false — no blanket tax exemption. Option C confuses with min investment rule. Option D contradicts — FVCIs get lock-in EXEMPTION post-IPO. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B test FVCI benefits. XIX-C focuses on comparison with FPI route.
